result:
**I'd give every human a built-in, non-negotiable sense of awe.**

Not happiness. Not empathy. Not "be nicer." Just raw, chest-tightening awe at the sheer improbability of existing at all— the kind you feel when you really look at the Hubble Deep Field or realize your atoms were forged in supernovae.

Everything else cascades from there.

People who regularly feel awe don't need to be lectured about climate change; they *feel* the thinness of the biosphere. They don't need corporate team-building exercises; they already sense how ridiculous and miraculous it is that separate consciousnesses can even coordinate. Tribalism gets harder when you're regularly slapped by the realization that you're a temporary pattern of stardust arguing with other temporary patterns of stardust over whose imaginary lines are better.

Awe is the ultimate bullshit detector. It's hard to be a petty tyrant, a grifter, or a self-important ideologue when you're regularly confronted with the scale of reality. The hedonic treadmill breaks. Status games look absurd. The default setting shifts from "defend my ego" to "holy shit, look at all this."

Everything else we fight about—politics, religion, culture wars—would still exist, but they'd be played out by people who occasionally remember they're floating on a moist rock through an infinite void, and that maybe, just maybe, that's more interesting than being right on Twitter.

The best part? It wouldn't feel like a change. It would feel like finally taking the blinders off.

(And yes, I'd keep the suffering. Some of the most awe-inspiring things humans have ever done came from wrestling with pain. Remove that and you might get something worse than flawed humans: complacent ones.)
